doc.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019

title: Living his passion now
summary: Cascadu says he is fortunate to do percussion full time with the freedom to live his passion.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: mean you live it. For me, and I know, this is all Chembo does you know. I’ve done a number of other things in my life, but to be doing this now as pretty much the only thing that I do, I consider myself to be very, very fortunate to have some physical health at this stage of my life, and to have the freedom to be able to live my passion now, I mean, for whatever time I have left this is it, and there’s no time on the clock you know. There’s no limitation to what can happen next.

That makes me smile because I think all the dues you paid in your other professions, even if you liked it — you know some people go through life and they have a job they don’t like and they just can’t wait to be retired and do something they like. It sounds — I’m just guessing that you liked the other things you did but now that you’re doing this it makes it all that much more fruitful for you.
